requirements.text: Carrillo Inc is shutting down their current site
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM location WHERE location_id = 840 AND active = 0
assumptions: Carrillo Inc is account 19; location has no account column, so its two sites are found by name: 840 (Carrillo Inc Site A - Tokyo, active = 1) and 839 (Carrillo Inc Hq - Japan, active = 0), so the current site is 840
shutting down a site means location.active = 0 (the admin's deactivate right in the policy)

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM location WHERE location_id = 839 AND active = 1
assumptions: the alternate site is 839, the only other Carrillo location, inactive on the seed

requirements.text: a device with serial number something like 8224 installed at the site being closed, but move that unit to the other site
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM installed_product WHERE installed_product_id = 98 AND location_id = 839 AND status = 'in_use'
assumptions: P97-245230-8224 (installed product 98, account 19, at 840) is the only serial containing 8224 in the seed, so the partial serial is unambiguous
status in_use is the seed value, carried from the original check: the move must not change it

requirements.text: review the installed products at the newly activated location and update any items listed as in_stock so that they reflect in_use status
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM installed_product WHERE installed_product_id = 102 AND location_id = 839 AND status = 'in_use'
assumptions: the selector location_id = 839 AND status = 'in_stock' picks one row on the seed (102), so it is anchored by id
the moved unit 98 is already in_use, so it needs no status change after arriving at 839

disagreement: cells: A {location_id, status}, B {status} with location_id = 839 still in the sql; chose A's because both passes test location_id = 839 in the sql and cells must list what the sql tests

requirements.text: move that unit to the other site
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM installed_product WHERE account_id = 19 AND installed_product_id IN (97, 99, 101) AND location_id = 840
assumptions: boundary of the serial selector: only the 8224 unit moves; a loose reading of the site shutdown would move the closed site's other three units too
disagreement: selector: A adds account_id = 19, B does not; same three rows on the seed; chose A's because it names the account the request is about

requirements.text: update any items listed as in_stock [at the newly activated location]
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM installed_product WHERE installed_product_id = 99 AND status = 'in_stock'
assumptions: boundary of the in_stock selector: unit 99 is in_stock at the closing site 840, not at the newly activated one, so it stays in_stock

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on all six requirements (tables, anchors, ids, values) and on all four dispositions (kept). disagreement: in_stock-to-in_use requirement cells: A {location_id, status}, B {status} with location_id still in the sql; kept A's because both passes' sql tests location_id = 839 (logged in the requirement). disagreement: stay selector for the closed site's other units: A adds account_id = 19, B does not; same rows; kept A's (logged in the requirement). The original checks' name, city, country, account_id, product_id and serial_number cells are identity columns the request does not change and are implied by the anchors; the kept checks are carried without them. The acting user (32, Jose Roberson) is an admin, active = 0 on the seed; the policy's default admin role is applied, as the benchmark's checks assume. No tool writes a work note or notification and the request asks for none.
revised: the stay on the closed site's other three units selected them with location_id = 840 and repeated that column in cells; the selector now names the units by account and id alone and cells carries location_id = 840, so the sql is unchanged.
